title: Cop Trapped in Fleeing Getaway Car Shoots Driver
description:
* (Disclaimer: The content in this video is intended for educational and informational purposes only)
Antioch, California — On February 20, 2026, at 5:16 a.m., Antioch Police Officers were dispatched to the 4500 block of Lone Tree Way after a report of an armed robbery in progress at a FoodMaxx groceries store. The suspect vehicle backed into the front of the store, breaking the glass doors. Three male occupants exited the vehicle and entered the store. A store employee reported one of the suspects was armed with a firearm and threatened him. Approximately three minutes after the suspect vehicle backed into the store, Antioch Police Officers  arrived on scene. The suspect driver, later identified as 23-year-old Dominick DeSouza, rammed his vehicle into an occupied patrol car. Officer Donaldson, on foot, reached into the suspect vehicle and engaged in a struggle with DeSouza. During the struggle, officer Donaldson was knocked into the suspect vehicle as DeSouza accelerated into the store and then drove forward at a high rate of speed. Two other suspects in the robbery fled the scene on foot. Officer Donaldson reached into the suspect vehicle and gave the driver, DeSouza, repeated commands to stop the car. 

DeSouza drove for approximately two miles while officer Donaldson repeatedly attempted to de-escalate the situation and persuade him to stop the vehicle. DeSouza repeatedly told officer Donaldson to "Get out" and said he was going to crash the car. DeSouza refused to stop to let the officer out and told him to jump from the moving vehicle. As DeSouza continued to drive recklessly through city streets, officer Donaldson informed DeSouza that he would be shot if he did not stop. DeSouza did not comply. Officer Donaldson discharged his service weapon. DeSouza crashed the car and ran into a neighborhood. Additional officers arrived on scene and located DeSouza about ten minutes after he ran from the car. DeSouza, Who sustained a gunshot wound to the leg, was found hiding in bushes and was taken into custody without further incident. Officers rendered medical aid until the arrival of paramedics. DeSouza was transported to a hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. DeSouza was charged by the contra Costa county district attorney's office with: Kidnapping Robbery, Assault With a Deadly Weapon Upon a Peace Officer, Grand Theft, Unlawful Driving or Taking of a Vehicle. Officer Donaldson suffered minor injuries during the incident. No other members of the public were injured.
